links.outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of ChatGPT-4o answers on SLE biologic therapy
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o FKGL 11.7 (or 14.9) and FRE 17.3 (or 11.7) versus Google FKGL 16.2 and FRE 20; both required college graduate-level reading proficiency, far above sixth-grade level.
links.quote: These results indicate that both texts have a high level of reading difficulty, requiring readers to have a college graduate-level reading proficiency [ 41 ].

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient information text
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o and Google answers had high reading difficulty requiring college graduate-level proficiency; a sixth-grade prompt improved FKGL from 11.7 to 10.5 and FRE from 17.3 to 51.9.
links.quote: However, the content’s readability was low.

links.outcome: Hallucination in ChatGPT-4o links and answers via two-step verification
links.effect: No hallucination found in links or answers after verifying links manually and checking accuracy scores (<3 = hallucination).
links.quote: No hallucination was found in the links or answers provided by ChatGPT after the 2-step verification.

links.outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4o answers rated by physicians on 6-point Likert scale
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o mean accuracy 5.83 (SD 0.49) vs Google 4.75 (SD 0.94); mean difference 1.08 (95% CI 0.61-1.54).
links.quote: In terms of accuracy, the accuracy scores indicate that ChatGPT-4o achieved a higher mean score (mean 5.83, SD 0.49) compared with Google Web Search responses (mean 4.75, SD 0.94), with a mean difference of 1.08 (95% CI 0.61‐1.54).

links.outcome: Comparison of ChatGPT-4o versus Google Web Search on accuracy and completeness
links.effect: ChatGPT-4o was more accurate (5.83 vs 4.75) and more complete (2.88 vs 1.68; difference 1.2, 95% CI 0.96-1.44) than Google Web Search.
links.quote: For completeness, ChatGPT-4o’s mean score was 2.88 (SD 0.32), significantly higher than Google Web Search’s 1.68 (SD 0.69), with a mean difference of 1.2 (95% CI 0.96‐1.44).
